statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 15 of 100 in the low band, ten points below the 25-point block threshold, because CME equity index futures remain inside the regular weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to be pathological. Nine of the twenty-four forward slots sit inside that closure. Stress rises to 68 in the high band: UKMTO reported a second vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz late Saturday with a fire and crew evacuation, alongside the Iranian cargo vessel hit near Qeshm with one dead, and a Russian drone struck a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border, after which Poland activated defence and reconnaissance systems while reporting no violation of its airspace. Crude above $100, a 10-year near 4.95 per cent and a Fed decision on Wednesday priced near an 85 per cent chance of a 25 basis point increase complete the backdrop. The one structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart, published as a narrow danger window running to 03:00 UTC on Monday rather than a broad session-wide state change.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in nine of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC on Friday for the weekend and are scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the weekend record has broadened to a second Hormuz vessel incident, but it is carried in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path currently exists to be pathological; the record also remains two-sided, with Monday's Gulf-Iran meeting in Oman on temporary Hormuz shipping arrangements set against the vessel strikes, and with Poland reporting no airspace violation and no Article 4 consultation. Third, the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than a broad shutdown, and even the peak conditional Tail of 24 stays one point below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this reading.
headline: CME equity index futures remain inside their scheduled weekend closure with the Nasdaq-100 still at Friday's 29,368.44 close and VIX at 15.84, while a second Strait of Hormuz vessel strike reported by UKMTO and a Russian drone hit on a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border add unpriced weekend exposure; Tail holds at 15 in the low band because no price path exists to be pathological, and the published risk is concentrated in the 22:00 UTC restart.
body:
Last observed tape. The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 29,368.44, up 0.91 per cent from a 29,103.51 previous close, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 day range, with a 52-week range of 22,841.42 to 30,762.20. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.71 intraday high. That was a relief session recovering part of the preceding decline, and it is two-sided, mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, which is why the published dominant mode is normal.

Cross-asset state. WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent on Friday, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent, the pullback following Iranian state media confirming that Tehran would meet Gulf states in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz; Brent still finished the week 9.7 per cent higher. H.15 for 10 September shows the 2-year Treasury at 4.56 per cent and the 10-year at 4.95 per cent, both higher across the week. Crude above $100 alongside a recovering equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting cross-asset signals raise Stress more than Tail. Delayed latest-session context is consistent with that reading: Nasdaq futures plus 0.86 per cent, VIX futures minus 8.41 per cent, seven of eight megacaps higher and a semiconductor mean of plus 1.75 per cent. That shared context file is flagged partial this hour because its calendar section failed to collect, so the macro calendar below rests on independent verification; the remaining sections are labelled delayed, latest-session context and are not treated as live price-path evidence.

Weekend record. Two independent vectors remain unpriced. In the Strait of Hormuz, an Iranian cargo vessel was struck early Sunday off Qeshm Island, killing one of its ten crew and injuring four, with the Qeshm governor blaming a terrorist enemy and the projectile unidentified; separately, UKMTO reported a further vessel hit by an unknown projectile late Saturday, with a fire that was brought under control and the crew evacuated. Gulf-state foreign ministers are due to meet their Iranian counterpart in Oman on Monday to discuss a temporary arrangement for managing shipping through the waterway, which is a genuine two-sided checkpoint rather than a one-way escalation. In Ukraine, a Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train roughly two kilometres from the Polish border in Volyn region during an overnight assault of 453 Shahed and Gerbera drones that killed six civilians and injured 43; Ukrainian Railways reported no injuries on the train because the crew had been warned in advance. Poland activated defence and reconnaissance systems and issued alerts in two border provinces, but confirmed no violation of Polish airspace and no injuries on the Polish side, and no Article 4 consultation has been called.

Why Tail stays low while Stress is high. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. With the reference contract shut, that path cannot exist, cannot be observed, and cannot be scored. Severe but unpriced headline flow, elevated crude, rising yields and an imminent policy decision are exactly the inputs that belong in Stress, which is why Stress is 68 in the high band while Tail is 15 in the low band. The published forecast caps conditional Tail at 19 for every hour inside the closure for the same reason.

Horizon and checkpoints. The single structural checkpoint inside the next twenty-four hours is the 22:00 UTC restart of CME equity index futures, published with a conditional peak Tail of 24 and a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC on Monday. No high-impact U.S. macro release falls inside the horizon; the calendar reloads on Tuesday with ADP and Empire State, and the FOMC decision, Summary of Economic Projections and press conference follow on Wednesday at 18:00 and 18:30 UTC, with market pricing near an 85 per cent chance of a 25 basis point increase after core PCE ran above 3 per cent every month this year. Those sit outside this horizon and are recorded in the event calendar rather than in the hourly path.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 13:00 UTC on 12 September to 12:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The whole window sits inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and every slot is green with EA_ON and a normal dominant mode. Tail held at 6 for the first sixteen slots, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00, 9 at 07:00, 10 at 08:00, 11 at 09:00, 12 at 10:00, 13 at 11:00 and 14 at 12:00 on 13 September, tracking elapsed time without price discovery rather than any observed structure. Stress traced a shallow U through Saturday, easing from 53 to 50 by 17:00 UTC before rebuilding to 53 at the futures-session boundary, then climbing steadily overnight from 56 to 67 as the Hormuz and Ukraine vectors accumulated. Confidence stayed in the high band throughout, between 85 and 87, because levels, yields, oil and the calendar were verified continuously even though no live price path existed to observe.
outlookSummary: Nine of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure; the reference contract is scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's tenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 15 in the current slot, the only slot describing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts to 19 by 20:00 UTC as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates across two independent vectors. It is capped at 19 through the closure because a shut contract cannot show the one-way structure Tail measures. The restart slot carries the horizon's peak at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, and five slots from 22:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC on Monday sit in that watch band, published as a narrow danger window to 03:00 UTC rather than a broad shutdown. From 03:00 UTC the path returns to the low band and decays through Asian and European hours to a horizon low of 13, on the conditional assumption that the weekend record reprices through an orderly two-sided auction. That assumption would be invalidated by a gapped restart that extends after failed retracements or holds near a session extreme. Stress peaks at 72 in the restart slot and eases to 58 by the final slot, staying elevated throughout on the unresolved Hormuz situation. Confidence declines from 86 to 73 across the horizon purely as a function of forecast distance from the last verified evidence. The U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC on Monday and Wednesday's FOMC decision both fall outside this horizon.
